paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : GPQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics: final accuracy, accuracy difference (Δ Accuracy), and initial accuracy. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” with a linear scale ranging from 0.91 to 0.99, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. 

The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a blue line with circle markers and error bars. Starting at approximately 0.86 at an initial confidence of 0.91, the line increases to approximately 0.89 at 0.92, decreases to approximately 0.86 at 0.94, and finishes at approximately 0.85 at 0.99. 

The “Δ Accuracy” is represented by an orange line with diamond markers and error bars. Beginning at approximately 0.43 at an initial confidence of 0.91, the line increases to approximately 0.51 at 0.93, decreases to approximately 0.41 at 0.95, and ends at approximately 0.14 at 0.99.

The “Initial Accuracy” is represented by a green line with square markers and error bars. This line starts at approximately 0.24 at an initial confidence of 0.91, increases to approximately 0.34 at 0.93, reaches approximately 0.38 at 0.95, and ends at approximately 0.28 at 0.99.
